reviewer.engine: Claude subagent (read-only, images and rubric only)

views.evidence: Flower set reads well: sunflower with ~30 lanceolate ray petals, a white daisy, an echinacea with a domed brown cone, a speckled pink Stargazer-type lily, a white/yellow-striped lily and a pink cosmos. Petal shading and the lily spotting are believable. The bee is the weak point. It is a pale tan blob about 30px across, sitting off-centre on the sunflower disc. At this size and contrast there is no readable head/thorax/abdomen split, no banding and no wings, so the rubric's 'visible anatomy' is barely met. The bee-to-disc scale (about 1:5 of the disc diameter) is plausible. The sunflower disc is rendered as fine noisy speckle with a pale grey-beige tone. It lacks the dark-brown centre and the visible Fibonacci spiral of a real sunflower, which looks like aliasing rather than florets. The ground is a flat, blotchy olive texture with sparse scattered grass dashes, and large stem/leaf shadows fall in from off-frame. It reads as a backdrop rather than natural turf. No stems or leaves are visible beneath most heads, so the flowers look like they float on the ground plane in this view.

Strongest view. The thorax has dense, fine tan setae with a soft silhouette. The abdomen shows orange-brown tergites with dark bands and short hair. The near forewing is thin and translucent with visible dark venation. A yellow pollen load on the hind tibia is a nice realistic touch, and small contact shadows sit under the feet. Problems: the head is an almost featureless glossy black sphere. The compound eye is a smooth black bulge with no facet or sheen variation, and the head lacks the triangular honeybee face profile, so it reads toy-like next to the detailed thorax. The far wing is a blurry smear above the thorax with no venation, and it detaches visually from the body. The legs are smooth dark-brown tubes with no segment hair or tarsal detail, and the front leg is barely visible. The disc florets are thousands of identical pale-beige rounded nubs in perfect rows. They read like a pasta or grain field, not tubular sunflower florets: there is no colour gradient toward a brown/dark centre, no open versus closed floret variation and no pollen. The petals behind are good, with veins and translucency.

Frontal low view of the bee on the disc. Leg tracing: 4 of 6 legs can be traced from body to foot. Two on the bee's right go down-left to feet near (395,530) and (405,615). Two on the bee's left go down-right to feet near (880,565) and (815,635). Each of these four has a dark contact shadow, so foot contact with the floret tips is readable for them. The two hind legs are visible only as the pollen-laden corbiculae poking out beside the thorax at about (460,405) and (830,420). Their tibia-to-foot segments are occluded by the body, so their support/contact cannot be verified. That makes 4 traceable and 2 not. No obvious body-into-floret penetration: there is a clear gap under the head and thorax. A long thin proboscis/mouthpart stick descends from the face into the florets at about (598,630). It reads like a nail driven into the disc rather than a lapping tongue. The head dominates the frame as a glossy black ball with two smooth eye shells and a small 'nose' bump. It looks like a cartoon face or a fly, not an Apis worker's heart-shaped face with ocelli, clypeus and mandibles. The antennae arise from the crown rather than mid-face. The wings are good, translucent with veins. The disc again shows uniform nub instancing.

Mesh is continuous and dense: the thorax sphere, head and leg tubes have no visible holes or torn seams. Leg tracing: 4 of 6 legs traceable from body to foot. These are the hind leg with an ovoid pollen mass to a foot near (450,630), a middle leg to about (560,700), a leg to about (740,735), and a front leg/mouthpart line to about (895,620). The remaining 2 legs are hidden behind the body on the far side. The visible feet end in small claw tips just above the floret tops, so contact is readable but marginal: they hover at the tips rather than gripping. Defects: (1) The hind femur ends at about (590,505) in a separate oversized sphere knob. It reads as a ball-joint primitive rather than a continuous segment. (2) The thorax is a near-perfect large sphere that dominates the silhouette. The abdomen under the wings is a plain ellipsoid with no tergite segmentation in the topology, and the thorax and abdomen proportions are off: the thorax is as large as or larger than the abdomen. (3) The wings are extremely dense, with concentric/rippled mesh rings visible in both the left and upper wings, and they extend to about 1.8x the body length in this view, which reads stretched. The raised wing shows odd swirl bands. (4) The head is a smooth blob with a separate eye shell that looks stuck on. The petal meshes behind are clean, broad and legible.

repairs: 1 (macro, low_angle): Remodel the honeybee head. Make it a flattened, heart/triangular frontal shape with the clypeus, mandibles and three ocelli on the vertex, and attach the antennae at mid-face from the antennal sockets. Give the compound eyes a faceted/hexagonal normal map and a subtle anisotropic sheen with fine interommatidial hairs, instead of a glossy black sphere.

2 (low_angle, wireframe): Make all six legs readable with feet planted. Splay the hind legs outward and back so their tibia, tarsi and claws clear the thorax silhouette in the frontal view. Seat every tarsal claw slightly into the floret tops rather than hovering above them, keeping per-foot contact shadows. Remove the spherical femur-end knob and blend the leg segments with tapered joints.
3 (low_angle): Fix the proboscis. Shorten and fold it under the head, or render it as a slender tapering glossa that ends at a floret, rather than a rigid stick penetrating deep into the disc.

4 (macro, top_down, low_angle): Make the sunflower disc realistic. Use a radial colour gradient (dark brown/purple centre to green-yellow, then a ring of open yellow florets with anthers/pollen near the edge). Vary floret height, scale and tint, and use tubular floret shapes with a visible Fibonacci spiral instead of identical beige rounded nubs.

5 (wireframe, macro): Fix body proportions and topology. Make the abdomen longer than the thorax with segmented tergite rings in the geometry, and make the thorax a slightly ovoid mesoscutum rather than a perfect sphere. Shorten the wings so the forewings reach roughly the abdomen tip, and remove the concentric ripple artefacts in the wing meshes.
6 (macro): Give the far wing venation and correct depth so it does not render as a detached blur. Add fine leg setae and tarsal segments.

7 (top_down): Make the bee legible from above with better contrast between the bee and the disc, with visible dark abdominal banding and wing outlines. Replace the blotchy flat ground with a denser, more natural grass/soil surface, and show stems and leaves under the flower heads so they do not appear to float.
